rationale: Generous to positive. Early Apollo motifs remain Apollo-centered, but the Passion analogue is supplied by Marsyas; NH explicitly reverses Apollo/Marsyas identities. No preserved 3-event Gospel-like ordered chain across one narrative witness; multiple myth/source jumps.

Generous to positive. NH explicitly calls Esau/Jacob intertwined reflections of Christ, John and Judas. Canonical Genesis supplies birth/rivalry/birthright/ladder sequence, while the decisive murder of Esau is imported from other sources. Role splitting and source hopping prevent a strong score.

Generous to positive. Martyrdom and heavenly vision are central, but in Ascension of Isaiah the life/death/resurrection/ascension seen in the vision belongs to the Lord, not to Isaiah. Critical resurrection material therefore requires role transfer; Christian composition supplies an explicit alternative generator.

Conservative control score. Ovid gives ominous foreshadowing, Eurydice's death, Orpheus's underworld descent, later Orpheus death and reunion. Death/recovery roles are split and the descent occurs before Orpheus's own death, so no Gospel-order chain of 3 events is credited.

Conservative control score. One continuous Genesis narrative preserves Joseph as protagonist: predictive dreams, brotherly hostility, death plot/pit, sale, displacement/suffering, exaltation, brothers bowing, and explicit remembrance of the dreams. NH's own Lost Gospels chapter assigns Joseph mainly to Joseph Volotsky / Dmitry-Mordecai rather than Christ.

Conservative control score. In Jeremiah 38-39 the same prophet predicts Babylonian capture; the message causes officials to demand his death; the king yields; Jeremiah is lowered into a cistern to die, rescued, remains confined, and the city is then captured as predicted. Prophetic genre is a plausible alternative generator.
